claims.evidence: All 25 titles are jellyfish cards (Jellyfish Diet/Stingers/Life Cycle/Sting Care...), but 'bantol' is not a jellyfish: Wolff's Dictionary of Cebuano Visayan has 'bantul n k.o. small, excellent eating fish with poisonous spines... and a frog-like face', and binisaya.com glosses bantol = stonefish (Synanceja verrucosa). Wolff's Cebuano jellyfish words are bukya, buruy (general name for jellyfish), bulbug, sabay, dangkalan. Corpus: bantol 0 bodies / 25 titles; dikya 42 Cebuano bodies (46 Tagalog bodies), and the bodies of these very cards say dikya (ffct-01826 'Ang dikya mokaon og gagmay nga mga mananap', ffct-03270, ffct-04714). A Cebuano-only child reads these 25 cards as being about a venomous bottom-dwelling fish.

'landok' is Ilocano for iron (Wiktionary lists Ilocano only; no Cebuano/Hiligaynon entry), it has NO entry in Wolff's Cebuano dictionary (0 occurrences of landuk/landok in the whole dictionary text) and none on binisaya.com. Corpus: landok 0 bodies / 12 titles; the concept words the bodies actually use are puthaw 440 bodies for iron (ffct-02360 title 'Kakulang sa Landok Anemya' -> body 'Kon kulang og puthaw ang lawas'), and bakal 42 / asero 22 for steel (ffct-24923 title 'Semento Piga Landok Hila' -> body 'gisagol... ang semento ug bakal'); Wolff: 'asiru n 1 steel'. Use puthaw on the iron cards (ffct-02360, ffct-20659, ffct-21586, ffct-23726, ffct-27998) and bakal/asero on the steel ones (ffct-20686, ffct-24923, ffct-25363, ffct-25944, ffct-26597, ffct-27285, plus ffct-27118 metals).

All 10 titles mean shivering/vibrating (Heat From Shivering, Chills Before Fever, Eardrum Vibrates With Sound), but 'kangi' is not a word: 0 standalone occurrences anywhere in Wolff's Cebuano dictionary (headwords or example sentences), no binisaya.com entry, no Wiktionary page in any language (404), 0 hits in the Bloom Cebuano books. The 99 'bodies' the prefix-matching tool reports are kangitngit (darkness). Corpus: kangi 0 bodies / 10 titles vs mokurog 58, pagkurog 35, kurog 8 bodies -- and the bodies of these exact cards say kurog (ffct-00120 'mangurog kung bugnaw kay ang pagkurog naghimo og init'; ffct-07483 'Ang pagkurog mao ang paspas nga paglihok sa atong kaunuran'). Wolff 'kurug' covers both senses, incl. machine vibration ('Ang kurug sa makina'), so pagkurog also serves ffct-09699 and ffct-16917.

Not a meaning error -- all 11 titles are about weight/heaviness and the root bug-at is transparent. But the attested noun is the gi-...-on / ka-...-on circumfix form: Wolff under bug-at gives 'ka-un, gi-un n 1 weight', and the beginners' textbook glosses 'gibug-aton = weight, heaviness'; bare 'bug-aton' has no dictionary entry. Corpus: bug-aton 0 bodies / 11 titles vs gibug-aton 295 bodies, kabug-at 78, bug-at 648. So 'Elepante sa Bug-aton' is a clipped 'sa gibug-aton' (and the adjectival uses, 'Bug-aton nga Butang', would standardly be bug-at). Normalising this is spelling/morphology work, out of scope here.

Genuine Cebuano for fast, and it delivers exactly what all 23 title_en say (Fast-Growing Kamote, Cheetah Fastest Land Runner, Sound Fastest in Steel). Wolff: 'laksi = laski' and 'laski a be fast, sprightly in doing s.t. Laski mulakaw, A fast walker... Mulaski (malaski) na siyang sugoon' -- i.e. the ma- form is attested. The bodies simply prefer a different lexeme: paspas 1693 bodies (kapaspas 100), laksi/malaksi 0 bodies. Title-only vocabulary, not an error.

Wolff: 'lumuy, lumuy a soft and delicate, not rigid. Lumuy nga tsiku, A soft sapodilla' -- lumoy is the modern o-spelling of that headword and means precisely 'soft', which is what all 18 title_en say (Soft Guyabano Spines, Hatchlings' Soft Shells, Soft Pure Gold, What Soft Water Is). Corpus: lumoy 0 bodies / 18 titles, humok 523 bodies (the bodies of these cards all say humok). Synonym, correctly used; absence from bodies is style, not meaning.

Standard Cebuano for sweat: Wolff 'balhas n 1 perspiration. 2 prickly heat. v perspire. Mubalhas ku ug mulampaso sa sawug, I'll perspire if I scrub the floor.' All 15 titles are sweat cards (Sweat Makes You Thirsty, Why Sweat Tastes Salty, Heat Stroke Stops Sweat). Corpus: balhas 0 bodies / 15 titles vs singot 115 bodies -- the bodies chose the synonym singot, but balhas is exact, not a defect.

Transparent, fully productive Cebuano agentive: tig- + sukod = 'the thing that measures'. The root is heavily attested in bodies (sukod 151, pagsukod 214, magsukod 27; Wolff has sukud and sukdanan 'thing on the basis of which other things are measured'), and the bodies of these cards say 'Ang rain gauge nagsukod...'. All 14 titles are instruments (13x Rain Gauge, 1x Seismograph), so 'Tigsukod sa Ulan' delivers exactly the title_en. Title-compact coinage on an attested root, not a meaning error.

Regular Cebuano abstract noun 'importance' from hinungdanon (important), which the bodies do use: hinungdanon 21 bodies, mahinungdanon 16 bodies (kahinungdanon itself 0 bodies / 11 titles). All 11 titles are exactly 'importance of / why X matters' (Why Weather Study Matters, DNA Importance, Importance of Constellations), so the word delivers the title_en. Bodies just never need the nominalisation because they are declarative sentences.

Spanish loan for blue, and every one of the 23 titles is a blue card (Blue Light Scattering, Blue Neptune, Red Green and Blue). Attested in real human-written Cebuano: it appears in the Bloom Cebuano children's books in this repo (bloom-ang-regalong-relo, bloom-pagluto). The bodies use the nativised spelling asul (203 bodies; Wolff headword 'asul a blue'), and azul 0 bodies -- same word, Spanish spelling. Per the FINE rule for Spanish loans, no change.

tiglilimpyo: 0 bodies / 10 titles. The unreduplicated form IS attested: tiglimpyo 2 bodies (ffct-07114 'makatabang sa kinaiyahan isip tiglimpyo!' = cleaning up carcasses; ffct-14799 'ang ihi mao ang nag-unang tiglimpyo sa dugo' = blood-cleaner), root limpyo 717 bodies. A token scan of every tig- form in the bodies shows the corpus never reduplicates the agentive: tiglimpyo, tighinlo (4), tighimo (2), tigbaligya (4), tigpanalipod (9), tigbantay, tigdala — zero tig-CVCV- forms. Meaning is delivered correctly: all 10 cards are cleaner fish/shrimp and their bodies say naglimpyo / maglimpyo / naglinis / paglinis (ffct-00877, ffct-09445, ffct-07766). Reduplicated spelling of an attested word, not a meaning error.

dako 2884 bodies / 270 titles vs daku 1 standalone body (ffct-32931 'human sa dakung pagsabog'). The daku root also surfaces inside body-attested derivations: padakuon, modaku, gipadaku (12 substring hits, e.g. ffct-04628 'modaku kung ngitngit'). Every example body renders the title's 'big/huge' as dako/dakong/dagkong (ffct-04197 'gamay nga mas dako', ffct-05550 'dako nga baba', ffct-10762 'dagkong kausaban'). Pure u/o spelling alternation, the same class as itum/itom. (Unrelated: ffct-03031 'Leon nga Daku nga Iro' also has iro=dog where the body says iring=cat — a different word's problem, not daku's.)

pagtatanom: 0 bodies / 9 titles; the unreduplicated pagtanom has 119 bodies / 18 titles and root tanom 2175 bodies. The word does deliver what the title_en says in every example — all nine are planting/replanting cards and their bodies use exactly this root: ffct-10111 'Ang pagtanom og narra', ffct-11694 'Ang pagtanom og kahoy, o reforestation', ffct-10950 'nagtanom pag-usab og mangrove', ffct-12185 'bag-ong tanom'. The only difference from the body vocabulary is the CV-reduplicated form, which the bodies never write. Spelling/morphological form, not a meaning error.

buhag: 0 bodies as a word, 9 titles. The 5 substring hits are a different word entirely — mobuhagay/mibuhagay 'gush/flow out' (ffct-03953 'dugo nga mibuhagay', ffct-30925 'mobuhagay ang lava', ffct-39839 'hinay mobuhagay ang honey') — so the corpus has no 'buhag' meaning 'makes'. The titles use it for two unrelated concepts at once, which is itself proof it is unanchored: 8 cards mean 'makes/builds' and ffct-01293 means 'blowhole'. For 'makes/builds' the corpus word is himo — 8906 bodies — and it is what these very cards' bodies say: ffct-11389 'naghimo og protina', ffct-05809 'naghimo og bag-ong red blood cells', ffct-04928 'ang bakterya nga naghimo sa nata', ffct-08170 'naghimo og daghang bitamina', ffct-14426 'maghimo og init'; the agent noun is tighimo. For the blowhole card the corpus word is lungag (323 bodies; across the 6 blowhole cards lungag is the body rendering) and ffct-01293's own body says 'lungag sa ibabaw sa ulo'. So ffct-01293 needs lungag and the other 8 need naghimo/himo; all 9 are wrong as written.

itom 259 bodies / 56 titles vs itum 0 standalone bodies. The itum spelling does occur inside a body derivation — ffct-07037 'Kon maitum nga yellow o orange ang ihi' — and the remaining substring hits are unrelated words (itumong 'aims', itumog 'dip', gitumban, gitumpok). All nine example bodies render the title's 'black' as itom (ffct-22657 'itom nga bado', ffct-23326 'ang atong makita itom', ffct-26053 'mukitag itom', ffct-26639 'itom ang kolor', ffct-12042 'Mas itom kini'). Textbook u/o spelling variant, explicitly out of scope.

liwang: 0 bodies as a word, 8 titles. The 2 substring hits are kaliwang = 'left (side)' (ffct-01321 'kaliwang baga', ffct-10019 'kaliwang ventricle') — a different word, and the wrong meaning for these cards. Every one of the 8 titles means light-in-weight, and every matching body writes gaan/magaan: ffct-05220 'Gaan kaayo ang lawas sa langgam', ffct-08443 'Ang balhibo sa langgam gaan apan lig-on', ffct-14967 'molutaw kung mas gaan kini', ffct-15485 'super magaan nga metal', ffct-16500 'mas gaan ang abo', ffct-00322 'Sobra kagaan ang ilang liso'. Corpus counts: gaan 546 bodies / 52 titles, magaan 60 bodies, vs liwang 0.

kagaangan: 0 bodies, 8 titles. The only gaan-family nouns the bodies actually use are kagaan / pinakagaan = 'lightness / lightest' (31 hits), so read as Cebuano the token says lightness, not reef. The corpus word for reef is bahura: 105 bodies / 28 titles, and it is the dominant Cebuano noun in reef cards (of 127 cards whose title_en contains 'reef', 70 bodies use bahura). Every example here proves it card-by-card — title says Reef, its own body says bahura: ffct-01127 'Ang bahura morag paril sa dagat', ffct-01180 'aron mahimo ang dagko nga bahura', ffct-03793 'naglibot ang reef shark sa bahura', ffct-08845 'manunukob sa bahura', ffct-11630 'Ang bahura sa korales', ffct-00444 'mobalhin sa bahura'.

punuan: 0 bodies / 8 titles; punoan: 189 bodies / 5 titles. Same word, same sense (stem/trunk), only the unstressed o/u differs — and each example body uses punoan for precisely the concept its title names: ffct-04574 'Ang berde nga punoan adunay chlorophyll', ffct-10155 'ang punoan sa saging', ffct-10625 'Ang punoan maoy nagdala sa tubig', ffct-11092 'Guwang sa sulod ang punoan sa kawayan', ffct-13593 'Ayaw isagol ang punoan ug gamot'. Spelling normalisation only, out of scope here.

kapeckan: 0 bodies, 0 English, 0 Tagalog, 8 titles — it is not a Cebuano word in this corpus in any form (no ka-pe... family member exists in the bodies; it looks like a mangled kapeligrohan). The corpus renders 'danger/dangerous' as peligro (281 bodies / 50 titles), delikado (326 bodies / 48 titles), katalagman (33 bodies / 23 titles) and kakuyaw (22 bodies), and those are exactly what these cards' own bodies say: ffct-02526 'pasidan-an ... kon adunay nagkaduol nga kakuyaw', ffct-15779 'Usa ka makahilo nga gas ... delikado kaayo', ffct-27838 'Delikado nga lamon ang gagmay nga magnetic beads', ffct-29260 'Ngano nga delikado ang PEIS Intensity VII'. Two of the eight are not even about danger — ffct-06876 is 'damage' (body: 'gidaot sa ilaga ang humay') and ffct-13041 is 'stored food saves lives' (body: 'kon wala nay makaon') — which confirms the token carries no stable meaning; all 8 titles are affected.

sipsik: 0 bodies, 8 titles. All 8 titles mean absorb/soak, and the corpus word for that is suyop — 565 bodies / 46 titles, and across the 496 cards whose English mentions 'absorb' the single most characteristic Cebuano body word is mosuyop (156 hits), followed by masuyop (36). Each example body says it outright: ffct-15882 'Mosuyop ang paper towel og tubig', ffct-16634 'mosuyop o mobalik sa kahayag', ffct-16849 'nagsuyop ug kainit', ffct-16862 'nagsuyop ug enerhiya', ffct-17768 'Mosuyop ang cotton og singot', ffct-31023 'mosuyop sila sa sobra nga tubig'. The near-spelling sipsip IS attested (65 bodies / 34 titles, e.g. ffct-06828 'sama sa espongha nga mosipsip ug motipig og tubig') and would also be readable, but sipsik with a final k is attested nowhere in bodies, English or Tagalog.

`--bis sugad` = 0 Cebuano bodies, 8 titles; absent from Wolff's Dictionary of Cebuano Visayan (accent/o-u-normalised search) and binisaya.com returns "No results found for the Cebuano word sugad" (nearest suggestions sugod/sukad/sugat). It is not the corpus's word for light: `--bis kahayag` = 1591 bodies / 442 titles, `--bis suga` = 341 bodies. Every one of the 8 cards' own bodies says kahayag, never sugad (ffct-23484 'ang kahayag mobiyahe sa tul-id nga linya'; ffct-23326 'ang itom mao ang kawalay kahayag'; ffct-23478 'Kon daghan ang gigikanan sa kahayag'), and the parallel TL titles all say Liwanag/Ilaw. Whatever 'sugad' is (it is the Waray/Bikol word for 'like, such as'), it does not deliver the 'Light' every title_en asserts.

`--bis pamalandong` = 0 bodies, 8 titles; `--bis palandong` = 0 bodies. Wolff lists it only under landung (shade/shadow) — 'palandung see landung' — i.e. the pamalandong family is mental contemplation/meditation, not optical bounce. The corpus renders optical reflection with the loan: `--bis reflection` = 36 bodies / 12 titles, reflect* = 130 bodies, `--bis repleksyon` = 3 bodies / 14 titles ('makita nimo niini ang repleksyon sa langit', ffct-23495), plus 'mobalik ang kahayag' (mobalik = 415 bodies). All 8 cards' bodies describe light bouncing — ffct-26858 'Ang reflection mao ang pagbalik sa kahayag gikan sa usa ka surface'; ffct-27913 'nag-reflect sila og kusog nga kahayag' — and the sibling Cebuano titles of the same 45-card EN-'Reflection' set already use Repleksyon sa Suga / Repleksyon sa Hayag. TL titles say Repleksyon/Pagsalamin. So the word delivers 'meditation' where title_en says 'Reflection'.

`--bis yabo` = 1 body and that single body means pouring/emptying, not fog: ffct-08616 'Ang pag-yabo sa tubig gikan sa mga sudlanan' (EN: 'Emptying water from containers'). Wolff's yabu is likewise 'throw/pour water' ('pirmihag yabu sa hinúgas'). The corpus's fog word is gabon: `--bis gabon` = 41 bodies / 17 titles, and `--en \bfog` shows gabon 40 occurrences as the top content word of the 68 fog cards (hamog 9, panganod 14). Each of the 8 cards' own bodies says gabon (ffct-30355 'Ang gabon gilangkuban sa daghan kaayong gagmayng tinulo sa tubig'; ffct-34846 'makahimo kini og baga nga gabon sa Baguio'), except ffct-32630 which uses hamog; none uses yabo. TL titles say Hamog/Ambon.

`--bis bukagnon` = 0 bodies, 7 titles; not in Wolff; binisaya.com resolves it only as root bukag 'basket' + affix -non, never as an insect. The corpus's bee word is putyokan/putyukan: `--bis putyukan` = 85 bodies, `--bis putyokan` = 50 bodies, `--en \bbee` ranks putyukan 101 / putyokan 72 / buyog 35 as the characteristic words of the 339 bee cards. All 7 cards' own bodies name the bee as putyokan/putyukan (ffct-01685 'mosayaw ang putyokan og espesyal nga sayaw'; ffct-13199 'Ang talo nga gigamit sa putyukan'), and the parallel TL titles all say Bubuyog. 'Bukagnon' does not deliver the 'Bee' of every title_en.

`--bis gatlang` = 0 bodies, 7 titles; absent from Wolff (o/u- and accent-normalised) and binisaya.com answers 'No results found for the Cebuano word gatlang' (it only offers the unrelated gutling). The corpus renders expansion gaps with gintang/puwang/luna: `--bis gintang` = 32 bodies / 4 titles, `--bis puwang` = 21 bodies, `--bis luna` = 139 bodies; `--en \bgap` ranks lungag 26, gintang 24, puwang 17, luna 17 across 129 gap cards. Every one of the 7 cards' own bodies uses one of those and never gatlang (ffct-15550 'may gagmayng gintang aron may luna sila molapad'; ffct-16795 'gagmayng puwang tunga-tunga sa mga riles'; ffct-15561 'may luna para sa paglapad'), and the TL titles all say Puwang. Note gintang is dictionary-attested ('May gintang dyis mitrus ang balay sa karsáda').

Spelling form of salamin, not a meaning error. `--bis salaman` = 0 standalone bodies (the 12 prefix hits are 'salamander', ffct-00707/ffct-01324), while `--bis salamin` = 193 bodies / 87 titles. Wolff's entry itself records variation — 'salamin, salaming n 1 mirror 2 s.t. made of glass', plus sámin = salamin — so the vowel is the only thing in play. Each of the 7 cards' own bodies spells it salamin for exactly the concept its title carries (ffct-23494 'Ang salamin tin-aw nga bildo nga adunay nipis nga sapaw sa makintab nga metal'; ffct-03363 'murag salamin nga moputos sa mga selula' = glass; ffct-27300 'Mosaka ang gecko sa hapsay nga salamin'), and all 7 parallel TL titles read Salamin. Meaning delivered; normalising the spelling is out of scope here.

Ordinary Cebuano of the simhot family that simply never surfaced in a body as a bare noun. The root is corpus-attested: `--bis simhot` = 10 bodies ('simhoton ang hangin', ffct-11019), and one of these very cards, ffct-11819, uses it in its own body — 'nakasimhot kini sa mga butang nga dili masimhutan sa tawo'. Wolff documents exactly this nominalisation under simhut: 'paN- v [A] smell, sniff' and, in the affix table, 'Panimhut, Sense of smell'. The corpus's habitual noun is the synonym panimaho (30 bodies, e.g. ffct-02635 'hait kaayong panimaho' for this card's own 'Pig's Sense of Smell'), which is word-preference, not contradiction: all 7 titles say Smell/Scent and pangimhot delivers smelling. TL titles confirm intent (Pang-amoy). No defect.

The root IS attested in bodies — the zero count is an exact-token artefact. `--bis paluya` = 4 bodies via its inflections: ffct-06527 'gigamit niini ang kuryente aron paluyahon ang isda', ffct-28138 'aron paluyahon ang gagmay nga isda', ffct-05859 'mahimong palig-onon, paluyahon, o pugngan ang mensahe' (EN 'stronger, weaker, or stopped'), dcard-10020 'babagan o paluyahon ang mosulod nga tsunami waves'. A prior pass in this same audit already accepted paluyahon on that evidence. Bodies also carry the family broadly (huyang 220 bodies, moluya/mohuyang). All 7 titles mean weaken/weakest and the bodies say exactly that (ffct-23723 'moluya kini'; ffct-24204 'mohuyang'); TL titles read humina/mahina. Compact title form of a corpus root.

Transparent -an derivation of a corpus word that delivers 'home', which is what all 6 title_en say (Home / Habitat / Houses). `--bis panimalay` = 41 bodies / 8 titles, and Wolff glosses the paniN- form as '1 household 2 home' ('Ang asáwa mauy hára sa panimalay'). The bodies' usual habitat noun is puy-anan (269 bodies / 93 titles, e.g. ffct-06142 'naguba ang ilang puy-anan' for 'Habitat Loss'), but preferring puy-anan over panimalayan is word-preference/register, explicitly out of scope — the title word still names a dwelling place, and the TL titles agree (Tahanan/Tirahan). No card is told something different from its English.

Exact-token zero only; the word is corpus-attested in its -un/-on form. `--bis kinhason` = 24 bodies, all shellfish ('kuhol, tahong, ug uban pang kinhason', ffct-00526; red-tide shellfish, ffct-00240; 'Asa mahiadto ang carbon sa kinhason?', ffct-00568 EN 'Where does carbon go in shells?'). Wolff lists kinhas as a headword under hunas — 'Manginhas ta kun muhunas, Let's gather shellfish when the tide is out' — so kinhas is the bare root of shellfish/shell-gathering. The 6 titles say Shells/Shellfish/Clams and the bodies use its co-hyponyms kabhang (143 bodies) / kabibe (50) / halaan; TL titles say Kabibe. Correct Cebuano that happens to be title-only.

'kasingkasin' 0 Cebuano bodies; 'kasingkasing' 317 bodies + 87 bis titles (+721 quiz-bank hits). Meaning is delivered — every example body itself says kasingkasing. All five ffct titles are exactly 20 characters ('Pitik sa Kasingkasin' 20, 'Lawak sa Kasingkasin' 20, 'Klima ug Kasingkasin' 20), i.e. the documented 20-char title-truncation bug (truncation_20char.py), a dropped final -g rather than a word choice. Route to the truncation fixer, not the word fixer.

'gibiya-ong' 0 Cebuano bodies, 0 of 27,783 quiz-bank items, 0 in the CPT Cebuano corpora — unsourced. The corpus word for weight/mass is 'gibug-aton' (295 bodies, 20 bis titles, 487 quiz) with 'timbang' (103 bodies, 52 weight/mass titles) alongside; all six example bodies use gibug-aton or timbang. The only attested biya- root in the corpus is gibiyaan = left/abandoned, which is not weight.

'sig-a' 0 bodies, but 'siga' 32 bodies and it is exactly the flame word: 31 of its hits fall inside cards whose English contains 'flame' (ffct-16088 'gamay nga siga sa kandila' = small candle flame; ffct-16002 'ang init nga hangin palibot sa siga' = hot air around the flame; ffct-05178 'walay siga' = no glow). Meaning matches all six title_en (candle flame / flickering flame / fire triangle). Hyphenated spelling form only.

'dagum' 0 bodies exact; 'dagom' 33 bodies and it means needle (ffct-02086 'talinis nga sungo nga morag dagom' = needle-like jaw; ffct-02263 talinis nga 'dagom' sa pino = pine needles; ffct-02626 'motuslok sa panit sama sa dagom'). The u-spelling is attested elsewhere in the same sense (ffct-29102 'dagumon nga porma sa dahon' = needle-shaped leaves; quiz-05709 'balahibo nga dagum-dagum'). Plain u/o spelling variation, meaning correct.

'energiya' 0 bodies; 'enerhiya' 702 bodies + 416 bis titles + 4,086 quiz-bank hits. Every example body itself writes enerhiya (ffct-22353 'dugangan kini og enerhiya', ffct-22361 'enerhiya gikan sa naglihok nga hangin'). g/h spelling of the same Spanish loan — the exact case named in the brief.

Absent from bodies (0 of 47,056) and from every Cebuano quiz-bank field; the corpus word for spine/backbone is 'gulugod' (63 bodies, 21 bis titles, 383 quiz), and the bodies of all five example cards use gulugod. But the word is not shown to be wrong: its only corpus occurrences (153 in the raw DepEd crawl, 1 quiz option) are TAGALOG, where taludtod = line of verse, and Visayan lexicons give taludtod/taludtud = backbone, ridge of the back — so it is plausibly compact title vocabulary for gulugod. No corpus evidence of a meaning error, so FINE per the unsure rule; flag for a native check rather than a rewrite.

'kuruy'/'kuroy' 0 hits in 47,056 Cebuano bodies, 0 in the 27,783-item quiz bank, 0 across the CPT Cebuano corpora — unsourced in any register. The corpus word for shiver/vibrate is 'kurog': 8 exact bodies, 34 'mokurog' hits inside cards whose English contains 'vibrat', 320 quiz hits, and other bis titles already use it (pagkurog 25, kurog 11). Each example card contradicts its own title — ffct-00451 body 'Mokurog ang lawas', ffct-23276 'nagkurog o naglihok dali balikbalik' — and their terms fields list kurog/pagkurog/nagkurog.

'dapit' in the corpus means place/spot or to adjoin — 576 body hits, all locational (ffct-00020 'Hugasi ang dapit', ffct-00082 'motubo sa laing dapit'), and quiz-04860 uses the exact form: 'nagdapit sa baybayon sa Pilipinas' = adjoins the coastline. It never means endangered. Endangered/threatened is 'nameligro' (47 bodies, 6 bis titles, 51 quiz) or 'namiligro' (34 bodies); all five example bodies use namiligro/nameligro while the titles say Endangered/Threatened.

'lagtaw' 0 hits in 47,056 bodies, 0 in the quiz bank, 0 in the raw and synthetic CPT Cebuano corpora — unsourced, and no near-spelling supports an 'adult' sense ('laktaw' = skip, 1 body, leap year). The corpus word is 'hamtong': 179 bodies, 163 hits inside cards whose English contains 'adult', 486 quiz, 8 bis titles; 'hingkod' (24 bodies) is the secondary. Every example body uses hamtong or hingkod, and the tl titles all say Matanda.

The corpus does use katkat — but for CLIMBING, never itching: 18 body hits (mokatkat 13, makakatkat 3, nagakatkat 1, pagkatkat 1) e.g. ffct-00520 'nagakatkat nga palma — mokatkat kini sa kahoy', and 42 quiz hits such as 'mokatkat sa makinis nga ibabaw' (climb smooth surfaces). Itch is 'katol' (18 bodies, 73 quiz), with kati (4 bodies) and pangatol. All five example bodies use katol/kati/pangatol against an itch title — ffct-02240 'kusog nga katol sa lubot', ffct-06845 'kati', ffct-12700 'pangatol'.

`tolog` 0 bodies / 5 titles; `tulog|katulog|matulog` 147 bodies, 62 titles. Pure u/o spelling alternation (same class as daku/dako) — binisaya.com resolves a query for "tolog" straight to the entry `tulog` = sleep. The tl titles say 'Pagdaloy ng Init' (pagdaloy: 32 tl bodies vs 2 bis), so pagdalag looks like a mangled carry-over of Tagalog daloy.

kurug: 0 Cebuano bodies, 4 titles. Same word as kurog, which the bodies use constantly — 8 bodies with the bare form, 140 with affixes (mokurog, mangurog, pagkurog) and 11 bis titles — for shiver/vibration/tremble. ffct-23164's own body says 'ang tinuod nga pagkurog nga mohimo sa tingog' under the title 'Bati ang Kurug sa Tunog'. This is the u/o alternation already ruled a variant (itum/itom, daku/dako), not a meaning error: every example delivers vibration/rumble as its title_en says. Normalising the spelling is out of scope here.

kit-an: 0 bodies as a standalone token, but the root is the corpus's own — makit-an appears in 286 Cebuano bodies ('makit-an ra kini sa Pilipinas'), makita in 1,927 bodies and 25 bis titles. All four titles are the frame 'X nga Dili Kit-an' = 'X that cannot be seen', which is exactly what their title_en says (Water Vapor Invisible, Oxygen Invisible Too, Sound Invisible but Real, Vapor Is Invisible) and exactly what their bodies say ('dili makita', 'invisible gas'). Compact title clipping of the corpus's own makit-an, delivering the right meaning; not a substitution.

pag-itom: 0 bodies as a token, but it is the regular pag- nominalisation of itom, which the corpus uses everywhere — 227 bis bodies, 49 bis titles — and the darkening sense is attested in verb form: moitom/mangitom (10 bodies, e.g. 'hinay-hinay nga mangitom') and pagngitom (ffct-17175 'Ang pagngitom sa daang plata'). 'Pag-itom sa Plata' delivers title_en 'Silver Tarnishing' and the body agrees ('Nganong moitom ang pilak'); 'Pag-itom sa Abokado' for browning is the same darkening sense the body carries ('paspas mongitngit'). Ordinary Cebuano that simply happens to be title-only.

daog: 0 bodies for the bare token, but the root is thoroughly attested in bodies with affixes — modaog 21 ('Modaog ang aninipot', 'modaog sa layo nga dagan'), nakadaog, and kadaugan (ffct-36655, the very card whose title is 'Walay Daog' / 'No Winner', body 'dili ang kadaugan'). dcard-03517's body says 'maoy modaog sa competition alang sa sunlight' under the title 'Daog sa Sunlight'. Bare-root title Cebuano meaning win/beat, which is precisely what all four title_en say (Lift Beats Weight, Pole Beats Gravity, No Winner, Winning the Sunlight).

kasubsob: 0 bodies, 4 titles, all meaning frequency. The root is the corpus's own word for 'often': subsob 17 bis bodies ('mas subsob molubad', 'mas masubsob na mahitabo', 'mokaon og subsob'), and dcard-05591 — one of these very cards — glosses frequency in its body as 'unsa ka subsob mahitabo ang usa ka butang'. ka- + subsob is a well-formed abstraction that delivers 'how often' for every example (Wave Frequency, El Niño Frequency, Asking About Frequency, Cat Heat Frequency). The bodies happen to prefer the English loan frequency (133 bis bodies, 56 bis titles; ffct-21961 glosses it 'frequency (kadalas)'), but preferring a loan in bodies is not a meaning error in the title.

Compound of two of the corpus's most common words: `adlaw` = 2851 bodies / 756 titles, `gabii` = 571 bodies / 133 titles. Bodies never hyphenate it because prose writes it out as a phrase — ffct-28853's own body: "adunay adlaw (day) ug gabii (night)", ffct-32043: "halos patas ang gitas-on sa adlaw ug gabii". The hyphenated form is title compaction of exactly that phrase, and it matches every title_en (Day/Night, Day-Night Cycle, Arctic Day & Night). Zero-body count is a formatting artefact, not a vocabulary gap.

`hamilog` = 0 Cebuano bodies / 4 titles, and it is absent from four independent sources: the 47,056-card pool, Wolff's *A Dictionary of Cebuano Visayan* (0 hits after accent-normalisation; its humidity/damp headwords are alimuut, hamlug/hamlig, umug, alingasa, tami), the CPT Cebuano corpus, and binisaya.com (which returns only an algorithmic affix parse ha-+bilog yielding 'matchstick/melon', not a headword). The corpus does have a word for this concept: `alimuot` = 3 bodies, and ffct-34685 glosses it explicitly — "Ang alimuot (humidity) o gidaghanon sa alisngaw sa hangin" — alongside `halumigmig` = 15 bodies and the English loan `humid` = 31 bodies. All four cards' own bodies use the loan ("mas humid ug mainit-init ang hangin", "Ang humidity sa Pilipinas moabot sa 80-90%"), and their Tagalog sides use mahalumigmig/maalinsangan — no cognate of hamilog anywhere in the card. The titles carry the humidity concept entirely on a word no Cebuano source attests.

Same lexeme, different glottal-stop spelling. `liki` = 92 bodies / 15 titles (+ `liki-liki` = 6 bodies); `lik-i` = 0 bodies / 4 titles. The four cards' OWN bodies spell it `liki`: ffct-32213 "nagpuyo sa mga liki sa mala nga yuta", ffct-32215 "kon naa nay liki ... modako ang mga liki", ffct-32217 "Dili hugaw ... ang liki-liki nga yuta", ffct-32218 "pagbantay sa lawom nga liki". Wolff confirms liki = crack ("buliti ug simintu ang liki" = fill the crack with cement). Meaning is delivered correctly in every title (Cracks / Cracked Ground); only the medial hyphen differs, so this is orthographic normalisation, out of scope here.

Over-suffixed gerund of a root the bodies use heavily: `pagpabugnaw` = 47 bodies / 17 titles, `pabugnawan` = 11 bodies / 3 titles, `pagpabugnawan` = 0 bodies / 4 titles. dcard-12583's own body uses the verb form the title over-nominalises — "pabugnawan ang bulb sa dili pa tipigan" — and dcard-04023's body has "kung pabugnawan, moubos ang temperatura". Wolff lists pabugnaw under bugnaw (cool). The form reads as 'the cooling of X' and delivers every title_en (Cooling Slows Molecules, Heating and Cooling, Cooling the Bulb); it is a morphological, not semantic, divergence from the corpus's `pagpabugnaw`.

`daug` means win/defeat, not trail. Wolff's entry: daug = 'overcome', 'prevail', 'vanquish', and as a noun the winnings ("bahina ang daug" = divide the winnings); binisaya.com gives win / overthrow / prevail / vanquish and no spatial sense. Exact-word count in the pool: `daug` = 0 bodies / 3 titles (the 17 prefix hits are `daugdaugon` = oppress, ffct-08017 "dili daugdaugon"). The corpus word for the concept is right inside these very cards' bodies: ffct-00295 "Ang kuhol magbilin ug sinaw nga AGI sa uhog" under title "Daug nga Lika sa Kuhol" / Snail Slime Trail; ffct-08253 "magbilin kini og tag-as nga AGI sa damuhan" under "Daug sa Dugong" / Dugong Feeding Trails; ffct-09038 "Ang mga TUNOB sa tiil nagpakita" under "Daug sa Kawan sa Dinosaur" / Herd Footprint Fossils. Corpus counts: `agi` = 49 bodies, `agianan` = 308 bodies / 80 titles, `tunob` = 18 bodies (Wolff: tunub = footstep, imprint). All three Tagalog sides use 'bakas'. Use `agi` for the two trail cards; `tunob` is the closer fit for ffct-09038's footprint fossils.

Final-/g/-dropping dialect form of `tubig`, which is the single most common content word in the corpus: `tubig` = 5700 bodies / 1279 titles vs `tubi` = 0 bodies / 3 titles. Each card's own body uses tubig: ffct-00523 "naangat sa tubig pinaagi sa taas nga tangkay", ffct-07026 "Ang ihi halos tubig ra". Wolff has no separate `tubi` headword; the clipped pronunciation is standard casual/Boholano Cebuano, i.e. dialect variation, which is explicitly out of scope for a DEFECT. Meaning (water) is delivered in all three titles. Worth noting ffct-07026's title "Ihi Tubi Tubig" carries both spellings at once, but that is a title-construction oddity, not a meaning error in the word.

ka-+lalum+-an abstraction of the standard 'deep' root, with the lalom/lawom l~w alternation that is ordinary Cebuano dialect variation. Wolff, under lalum: "ka- n depth, deepness ... dili masukud ang kalalum sa iyang gibati", plus kahi-an/kahiladman = depths. Pool counts: `kalaluman` = 0 bodies / 3 titles, but `kalalom` = 5 bodies / 4 titles (ffct-32231 "Mikatag ang enerhiya niini sa tibuok kalalom sa tubig"), `kalawman` = 1 body (ffct-09314 "nagsiga sa kalawman", EN 'deep-sea glower'), `kahiladman` = 13 bodies, `lalom` = 19 bodies, `lawom` = 378 bodies. The three cards' bodies all render the concept as "lawom nga dagat" and the titles all mean the deep sea (Deep-Sea Pressure Adaptations, Deep-Sea Giant Isopod, Darkness of the Deep) — meaning delivered; only the spelling/derivation differs from what bodies use.

Ordinary Cebuano that simply never lands in a body. Wolff: "langtaw v [an13; a2] see, look at s.t. in a distance. lantawa ang bukid ... nalantawan ku sa akung gitindugan ang pag-abut niya", with "lantaw = langtaw" cross-referenced and the idiom "naglantawg naglayag" = sits idly by watching; binisaya.com gives lantaw = foresee / overlook (have a commanding view). `paglantaw` = 0 bodies / 3 titles only because the bodies reach for `pagtan-aw` = 128 bodies / 14 titles and `tan-aw` = 23 bodies instead — a lexical preference, not a correctness gap. It fits all three cards: the heron and kingfisher titles are about a bird watching and waiting (bodies: "dili molihok samtang naghulat", "maghilom og dugay"), and "Kinatibuk-ang Paglantaw sa Meiosis II" is the idiomatic Cebuano for 'Meiosis II Overview'.

Clipped half of the reduplicated bird name. Wolff: "ngiwngiw n k.o. grass owl: tyto capensis"; there is no standalone `ngiw` headword in Wolff and 0 in the pool's bodies (3 titles). The bodies do use both full forms: `ngiwngiw` = 13 bodies / 6 titles (ffct-01461's own body: "Mangayam ang ngiwngiw sa gabii") and `bukaw` = 22 bodies / 9 titles, which is what ffct-01327 ("Makatuyok ang bukaw sa iyang ulo") and ffct-12960 ("Nganong hilom molupad ang bukaw?") actually say. All three titles mean owl and are read as owl; only the truncation is non-standard, so this is a spelling normalisation, not a meaning error.

Truncated spelling of the attested wasp word. Wolff: "tambubuan n k.o. large wasp"; binisaya.com gives tambuboan/tambubuan as the Cebuano for 'wasp'. The pool has it once in a body — ffct-14165 "allergic sa paak sa buyog o tamboboan" (EN: 'allergic to bee or wasp stings') — while `tambubuk` = 0 bodies / 3 titles. The corpus's dominant wasp word is `putakti` = 35 bodies / 9 titles (ffct-00223 "Ang hornet usa ka klase sa putakti"), which is exactly what ffct-05084's own body says under the title "Dakong Tambubuk" / Hornet Wasps. Meaning (wasp) is delivered in all three titles, so not a DEFECT — but flag that the truncation collides with Wolff's "tambubukag = hambubukag", a flying lizard (Draco sp.), so `putakti` or `tamboboan` is the unambiguous form.

lihog: 0 Cebuano bodies. Word-boundary grep over 47k bodies, the quiz bank and 11MB of Cebuano CPT text finds the root ONLY inside 'palihog' (= please / ask a favour; binisaya.com has palihog and lihogan, no plant sense). The corpus word for stem/stalk is punoan (189 bodies) / tangkay (104), and each of these three cards' OWN body uses punoan: ffct-01646 'tubig sa punoan', ffct-12822 'Ang punoan sa kangkong hungkag sa sulod', ffct-37862 'kabag-on sa pangunang punoan'. So 'Lihog sa Kangkong' reads as 'Kangkong's favour', not 'Kangkong Stems'.

matarong: 0 Cebuano bodies. binisaya.com gives only 'righteous / upright' — no sharpness sense — and the project's own Cebuano quiz text uses it adverbially for 'properly' ('dili nila matarong og hilis ang pagkaon' = 'can't properly digest'; 'atop nga wala matarong og taod' = 'roof not properly installed'). The corpus word for sharp is hait (236 bodies), and all three cards' own bodies use it: ffct-02597 'hait nga ngipon', ffct-13345 'pinaka-hait', ffct-32728 'Grabe ka hait kini'. Titles therefore say 'Righteous Teeth / Righteous Obsidian' where title_en says 'Sharp'.

gupos: 0 Cebuano bodies, 0 in the 27k-item quiz bank, 0 in 11MB of Cebuano CPT text, no entry in binisaya.com (it suggests gapos 'bind' / gupok 'crumble') and no Cebuano Wiktionary entry — unsourced everywhere except these 3 titles. The corpus renders 'clot' as mamuo/namuo (23 + 6 bodies, e.g. 'Ang dugo namuo aron sirhan ang samad' = 'Blood clots to seal a wound'), and each card's own body does exactly that: ffct-03002 'dali nga mamuo ang dugo', ffct-05592 'mokuyom ang dugo', ffct-06049 'ang imong dugo mamu-o'. 'Gupos nga Dugo' delivers no clotting sense.

alumindig: 0 Cebuano bodies, 0 in the quiz bank, 0 in the Cebuano CPT corpus, and no entry in binisaya.com or Wiktionary Cebuano (binisaya suggests alimatok, alindasay…). It exists only in cardsPool titles. The corpus word for wasp is putakti (35 bodies; 51 occurrences across the 46 wasp cards; 'Ang hornet usa ka klase sa putakti' = 'A hornet is a type of wasp'), and all three cards' own bodies say putakti: ffct-04292 'salag sa putakti', ffct-08398 'duha ka matang sa putakti', ffct-14885 'Kung matuslok ka sa putakti'. So the title names nothing a reader can identify as a wasp.

Same lexeme as the attested body word panimaho (30 bodies; binisaya analyses it as pani- + maho from baho 'smell'), with the pang- allomorph instead of pani-. The cards' own bodies use panimaho / pagpanimaho / masimhotan for exactly the concept the titles name ('Sense of Smell'), e.g. ffct-03510 'Hait kaayo ang panimaho sa reef shark'. Meaning is delivered correctly; only the affix spelling differs, so normalising it is out of scope.

Ordinary Cebuano that simply never reached a card body. binisaya.com defines bungdo as 'mound, pile' (synonym bundo) — exactly what title_en says ('Termite Mounds', 'Prairie Dog Mounds'). It is attested outside the card bodies: the Cebuano quiz bank uses it for bumps/mounds ('gagmay nga mga bungdo' = 'tiny bumps' in the friction items; 'pormang tasa, lungag sa yuta, bungdo' for nest shapes) and the Cebuano CPT text uses it for the Chocolate Hills. Bodies happen to prefer punso (3) / bunton (4) / bungtod, but that is word-preference, not a meaning error.

0 card bodies, but attested with exactly this sense in the project's other Cebuano text: the El Nino item in factoids-EARTH_SPACE-src.jsonl / quiz-lane / quiz bank reads 'Sa panahon sa El Nino, humoy ang upwelling' against English 'upwelling weakens'. That matches all three titles (weaker body, quality weakens, batteries wear out). Bodies prefer huyang (220) / maluya (41) / moluya — a preference, not a contradiction — and nothing in the corpus or dictionaries shows humoy meaning something else, so the DEFECT bar (word does not deliver title_en) is not met.

Regular Cebuano superlative kina-…-an of magulang 'elder', and attested in the project's Cebuano quiz bank for a real age-superlative: 'Ang kinamagulangang lalaki sa panon' against English 'The oldest male in the herd'. It does deliver 'oldest'. The bodies simply prefer other words for age superlatives — pinakatigulang (16 occurrences across the 71 'oldest' cards) for living things and labing karaan / kinakaraan (karaan 287 bodies) for rocks, as these very cards do (ffct-02428 'pinakatigulang buhi nga kahoy', ffct-39566 'labing karaan nga mga bato'). Personifying 'eldest' for a rock is register, which is out of scope.

Compact title compound of two fully attested body words: bitin = snake (127 bodies, e.g. ffct-00387 'Wala gyoy tiil ang bitin') and dagat. The very cards in question spell the same thing out in their bodies as 'bitin sa dagat' (ffct-05846 'ang ilong sa bitin sa dagat', ffct-12324 'Ang tinuod nga bitin sa dagat manganak'), and the trilingual quiz bank uses the hyphenated form too. Only the hyphenated spelling is body-absent; the meaning ('Sea Snake / Sea Krait') is exact.

binisaya.com lists mokita itself, parsed as 'mokita - kita - mo-~', and the root kita carries the sense 'see'. The corpus uses the same root throughout for seeing — makakita 341 bodies, nakakita 49, makita — including in these cards' own bodies (ffct-04625 'una nakakita sa bakterya', ffct-13043 'Makakita gihapon'). The difference is the mo- affix/aspect rather than a different lexeme, i.e. grammar-register, which is out of scope; the concept 'see' is delivered.

paggik: 0 bodies, 3 titles. paggiik: 2 bodies (ffct-14029, ffct-20103) -- and ffct-14029's OWN body says 'gitawag paggiik' while its title says 'Paggik'. All three TL titles are 'Paggiik'. Same word, one dropped 'i' (root giik/giok; 'giok' 7 bodies). Threshing is delivered correctly; spelling only.

uson: 0 Cebuano bodies, 0 en/tl/terms -- 3 title-only occurrences, and it is not a Cebuano word. The titles need 'again/re-' (TL titles read 'Muli', 'Muling Bubukas'). The corpus renders that as usab (2,074 bodies) or pag-usab (517 bodies) / balik (564 bodies), and these very cards' bodies do so: ffct-04758 'makatubo pag-usab', ffct-05444 'mabuka pag-usab', ffct-08062 'motubo balik'. Sibling titles confirm the house form: dcard-03534 'Pagtubo Pag-usab sa Nawala' = 'Regrowing Lost Parts'. 'Motubo Uson' delivers nothing.

simud: 0 bodies, 3 titles. simod: 16 bodies ('Kusgan ang simod sa baboy nga morag pala' ffct-01047), and ffct-07453's own body writes 'simod' under the title 'Simud'. Plain u/o variation (cf. daku/dako); meaning 'snout' is correct (TL 'Nguso'; corpus also uses nguso 11 / ilong 171).

panagupod: 0 bodies, 3 titles. The corpus noun for a group is grupo (318 bodies; 98 hits across 'group of' cards), pundok (44), panon (36) -- and the root upod is 0 in bodies, where uban (1,973) is used instead. But panag- is productive in the bodies (panag-uban, panaghiusa, panagtinabangay, panag-away), and panag-upod = 'being together / grouping', which is in the same semantic field as the title_en ('Grouping by Shared Traits', 'a Group of Fish'). upod vs uban is regional word-preference (Bohol/Hiligaynon-leaning), which is out of scope, so this is an unusual choice rather than a meaning error.

pamaaging is just pamaagi + the regular -ng linker. pamaagi: 50 bodies, 31 titles ('Lain-laing pamaagi ang gamiton sa bakawan' ffct-00528; paagi 474 bodies). The enclitic -ng on vowel-final words is normal in the bodies themselves: dakong 240 bodies, gamayng 168. 'Pamaaging Kaingin / Crisscross / Siyentipiko' = method/way, exactly what the title_en and TL ('Pamamaraang/Paraang') say. Tokenisation, not vocabulary, put it on the unattested list.

gadak: 0 bodies (and 0 in en/tl/terms), 3 bare-'Gadak' titles. The titles need the noun 'size' (TL 'Laki', 'Kasinglaki'). The corpus word is gidak-on: 365 bodies / 90 titles -- including these same cards' own bodies: ffct-06272 'Lainlain ang gidak-on sa mga dinosaur', ffct-16563 'parehas og gidak-on', ffct-07623 'sama ra kadako sa kamot' (kadak- 170 bodies). Bare 'gadak' is not a word in this corpus or in Cebuano: the root dak- always carries affixation (dako 1,777, dagko 825, gidak-on, kadako). Two sibling titles even write it out as 'Gadak-on' (ffct-16756, ffct-17114), showing 'Gadak' is the clipped form -- the known mid-word title-truncation signature.

manunod: 0 bodies, 3 titles. The corpus prefers the patient-focus forms mapanunod (11 bodies: 'Mapanunod nimo ang mga kinaiya...' ffct-01446) and napanunod (25 bodies), plus maipasa. But manunod is genuine Cebuano from the same root panunod (m-/pan- actor form, 'to inherit'), so 'nga Manunod' does deliver the inheritance sense the title_en and TL ('Namamana') ask for. The gap is voice/grammar preference (manunod vs mapanunod), which is register and out of scope.

dagkot: 0 bodies (0 anywhere but the 3 titles). All three titles mean 'thick' (TL 'Makapal' in each). The corpus word is baga: 859 bodies, 110 titles, and 487 occurrences across the 651 cards whose English contains 'thick' (--en thick ranks baga first, nipis second). Each of these three cards' own bodies uses it: ffct-06731 'baga nga panit', ffct-22698 'Mas baga ang insulasyon', ffct-23565 'baga ug gahi nga bungbong'. dagkot is not 'thick' in Cebuano (it is to light/kindle a fire), and it is not the plural dagko (825 bodies, 'big'), so 'Dagkot nga Bungbong' does not say 'Thick Walls'.

mubos: 0 bodies, 3 titles -- but moubos is attested 59 bodies ('mogawas ang kainit ug moubos ang temperatura' ffct-00425) and ubos 945 bodies. mo-/mu- is ordinary Cebuano vowel variation in the verbal prefix, so mubos = moubos, 'goes down / drops', which matches the title_en and TL exactly ('Pressure Drop' / 'Bababa', 'Bumaba', 'Kumokonti'). The bodies phrase it as 'mas ubos ang presyon' (ffct-18412), 'mokunhod ang presyon' (ffct-18438), 'Nagkagamay ang seagrass' (ffct-06861) -- same meaning, no error.

banyawak: 0 bodies, 3 titles. bayawak: 39 bodies, 35 titles -- and all three of these cards' own bodies write 'bayawak' ('Ang bayawak makatabang sa kinaiyahan...' ffct-07091), with TL titles 'Bayawak'. An intrusive -n- spelling of the same monitor-lizard word; the animal named is correct.

'iska' = 0 Cebuano bodies (the only near-hits are 'iskala' = scale), 3 titles; 'isda' = 883 Cebuano bodies / 273 Cebuano titles. All three cards are about fish and their own bodies say isda ('usa ka panon sa isda' ffct-07953; 'ang isda, nokos, ug pasayan' ffct-13819; 'makadaot kini sa mga isda' ffct-16191). The parallel Tagalog titles of the same cards spell it correctly: 'Kawan Isda Lito Predator' (ffct-07953), 'BFAR Isda Bituga Kabibe' (ffct-13819), and the terms fields list 'isda'. d>k is not a Cebuano spelling alternation, so this is a corrupted token, not a variant.

The attested spelling 'guwang' occurs in 31 Cebuano bodies and every one means HOLLOW, not swollen: 'gahi ang guwang niining punoan' (hollow bamboo stem, ffct-00401), 'guwang nga bukog sa langgam' (hollow bird bone, ffct-00557). 'gwang' itself = 0 bodies / 3 titles. All three titles need swollen/inflated, and their own bodies use hubag: 'Kon nahubag na ang butete' (ffct-08898), 'Manghubag ang mga glandula sa aping' (ffct-09120), 'mohubag ang butete' (ffct-12826). hubag = 14 exact / 124 substring Cebuano bodies, 12 titles; the cards' terms fields literally list 'hubag'/'namaga' and the tl titles say 'Namagang Butete', 'Beke Namamagang Pisngi'. Hollow is the wrong sense in all three.

Ordinary Spanish loan for 'friend', which is exactly what all three cards need (shrew/egret as friend of the farmer; talking with friends at 60 dB). Bodies use higala (36 Cebuano bodies) and all three bodies say higala, but amigo is not a meaning error and Spanish loans are explicitly in scope for FINE. Title-only absence here is a stylistic preference, not a defect.

kina- superlative on the attested root 'tig-a' (hard): tig-a = 6 exact / 83 substring Cebuano bodies, e.g. 'ang kidney stones mga tig-a nga tinapok sa mineral' (ffct-01789), and 17 Cebuano titles. Delivers 'hardest' on all three cards. The bodies simply prefer a different lexeme for the same idea — in the 'hardest' cards the Cebuano bodies use pinakagahi (35) / labing gahi (gahi = 870 substring bodies) — which is preference, not a meaning failure. The bare kina- form (vs corpus kina-...-an shapes like kinadak-ang, kinatas-ang) is a morphology/register matter, out of scope.

'ayang' = 0 Cebuano bodies, 3 titles; it is unattested anywhere in the corpus as a word (the 6 Tagalog body hits are all inside 'kaaya-ayang'). The Cebuano prohibitive is ayaw: 294 Cebuano bodies / 72 Cebuano titles, and all three of these cards' own bodies open with it — 'Ayaw pagsulay paglimpyo o pagluto og butete' (ffct-13040), 'Ayaw paghulog ang karaang baterya' (ffct-25077), 'Ayaw gyud og tan-aw og diretso sa Adlaw' (ffct-28942). The tl titles use 'Huwag'. There is no attested Cebuano prohibitive 'ayang', so the safety word these titles depend on ('Never…', 'Don't…') is not delivered.

Plain u/o spelling alternation of an attested word: kalalom = 5 Cebuano bodies ('Ang kalalom sa kolor ang nagsulti' ffct-17183; 'unsa kalalom kini' ffct-29811) and 4 titles; root lalom = 19 exact / 526 substring bodies vs lalum 10 substring. Meaning (depth / the deep) is delivered correctly on all three cards, whose bodies use the same root family ('kinahalawman nga bahin sa dagat' ffct-13073) alongside the more common lawom (378 bodies). Not a meaning error; normalising the spelling is out of scope.

'sirhi' = 0 Cebuano bodies / 3 titles. In Cebuano sirhi is the imperative of sira/sirado — 'close it' (sirado = 70 bodies, all sealed/closed senses, e.g. 'sirado nga babag' ffct-01392) — not 'destroy/break down'. All three titles need destroy/break down, and each card's own body uses the guba family: 'Ang atay kasagaran moguba sa tambal' (ffct-13500), 'gub-on kini sa asido ug enzyme sa tiyan' (ffct-13668), 'mawad-an kini sa kusog… mahimong dili na magnet' (ffct-22086). Counts: moguba 40, gub-on 34, guba 57 exact / 493 substring Cebuano bodies. The tl title 'Atay na Sumisira ng Gamot' shows Tagalog 'sira' was carried into Cebuano, where it does not carry that sense.

maka- + the core attested root tugnaw (cold): tugnaw = 60 exact / 227 substring Cebuano bodies, 24 titles; katugnaw = 76 bodies. 'Makatugnaw' reads as 'makes you cold / cooling', which is what all three sweat-cooling titles need. The corpus's ordinary counting form is 'duha ka' (1520 bodies), so duhang is just the tighter title form, not a different meaning: 'Duhang Fault' = two faults, 'Duhang Kinaiya sa Kahayag' = dual nature. Ligature choice is register, which is out of scope.

All three cards' own bodies spell it without the diacritic ('adunay makita nga liki o pingas', 'makakita ko og liki sa glass beaker'), so the meaning 'crack' is delivered exactly. Normalising the diacritic is out of scope here.

pang- + labay is attested in a body: dcard-07351 'ang gagmay nga particles nga gitawag ug ash ipanglabay ngadto sa hangin' = 'are thrown out'.
